In Retail & Consumer Goods, agentic ai & hyperautomation turns knowledge work into orchestrated autonomy. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: agentic process automation, digital workforce & multi-agent orchestration, decision intelligence systems — delivered on Dataq Swarm and Dataq Nexus and Dataq Compass with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Replenishment and allocation by rules of thumb
Store allocation, DC replenishment and size-curve decisions run on legacy heuristics; phantom availability and overstock coexist across the network.
Supplier collaboration by email
PO changes, OTIF exceptions and forecast sharing run on email chains; supplier risk surfaces as missed deliveries.
Demand signals too slow
Batch demand models react to last week; promotions, weather and local events shift baskets daily. Markdown decisions and replenishment both inherit the lag.

Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Every program of this type runs the same weekly rhythm, so your team can plan around it. The first quarter of the rhythm is verification: weeks 1–2 measure the current metric with your team and lock it by signature. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with your control owner receiving evidence weekly. Weeks 9–12 industrialize: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and the measured delta against the signed baseline. Gates are binding: miss one and the program stops or redirects with a documented decision.
